newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Afghan turmoil threatens Iranian security - Velayati.
newsitem.headline: Afghan turmoil threatens Iranian security - Velayati.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Tuesday the turmoil in Afghanistan threatened Iran's national security and that of the former Soviet republics of Central Asia.
"What's going on in Afghanistan affects our national security and that of the whole (Central Asian) region," visiting Velayati told Reuters after meeting Kazakh Foreign Minister Kasimzhomart Tokayev.

Velayati is at the start of a lightning tour of the Central Asian republics to discuss the situation in Afghanistan, where government forces are battling Taleban Islamic militia who drove them out of the capital Kabul late last month.
Iran and the former Soviet republics of Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan border Afghanistan.

Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan said after a meeting in Almaty earlier this month that they would take unspecified measures to prevent the Afghan war from spilling over onto their territories, but would not interfere in the conflict.
"Since the beginning of the new developments in Afghanistan, we have been in close contact with the Central Asian states," Velayati said.
Iran recognises the ousted government of Burhanuddin Rabbani, driven out of Kabul by the Taleban. Iranian media have condemned Taleban as manipulated by the United States, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
Iran is anxious to build its influence in oil-rich Central Asia, particularly in the sphere of oil and gas export routes out of the landlocked region.
The Iranian foreign minister visited neighbouring Kyrgyzstan earlier on Tuesday and is scheduled to travel to Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and India this week.
